name: Tyrannosaurus
fact: Tyrannosaurus rex lived in western North America at the very end of the Cretaceous. It had one of the strongest bites of any land animal.

name: Triceratops
fact: Triceratops had three horns and a great bony frill. It lived in herds, browsing low plants.

name: Edmontosaurus
fact: Edmontosaurus was a duck-billed dinosaur with hundreds of grinding teeth for chewing tough plants.

name: Ankylosaurus
fact: Ankylosaurus was covered in bony armour plates and swung a heavy club at the end of its tail.

name: Alamosaurus
fact: Alamosaurus was a giant long-necked titanosaur that lived in what is now the southwestern United States.

name: Titanosaur
fact: Titanosaurs were the last great long-necked dinosaurs and lived on almost every continent.

name: Abelisaur
fact: Abelisaurs, such as Carnotaurus and Majungasaurus, were short-armed predators of the southern continents.

name: Velociraptor
fact: Velociraptor was about the size of a turkey, covered in feathers, and lived in the deserts of Mongolia.

name: Hadrosaur
fact: Hadrosaurs were plant-eaters that walked on two or four legs. Some had hollow crests for calling.

name: Quetzalcoatlus
fact: Quetzalcoatlus was a pterosaur, a flying reptile, with a wingspan of about 10 metres, as wide as a small plane.

name: Ornithomimus
fact: Ornithomimus looked a little like an ostrich and was one of the fastest dinosaurs.

name: Protoceratops
fact: Protoceratops was a sheep-sized horned dinosaur from Mongolia, often found fossilised near Velociraptor.

name: Mosasaur
fact: Mosasaurs were huge marine reptiles, not dinosaurs, that swam in Cretaceous seas.

name: Early horse
fact: The earliest horses were the size of a fox and had several toes on each foot.

name: Mastodon
fact: Mastodons were distant relatives of elephants that browsed on trees and shrubs.

name: Terror bird
fact: Terror birds were tall flightless predatory birds that lived in South America.

name: Giant ground sloth
fact: Giant ground sloths could be as big as an elephant and stood on their hind legs to reach leaves.

name: Glyptodon
fact: Glyptodon was a car-sized relative of armadillos with a domed shell.

name: Woolly mammoth
fact: Woolly mammoths had thick fur, small ears and a layer of fat. A few survived on Wrangel Island until about 4,000 years ago.

name: Woolly rhinoceros
fact: Woolly rhinoceroses grazed the cold steppes of Europe and Asia. Ice Age artists painted them in caves.

name: Giant deer
fact: The giant deer Megaloceros had antlers up to 3.6 metres across.

name: Cave bear
fact: Cave bears were large bears that ate mostly plants. Their bones are found by the thousands in European caves.

name: Cave lion
fact: Cave lions hunted across the Ice Age steppe from Europe to Alaska.

name: Smilodon
fact: Smilodon, the sabre-toothed cat, had canine teeth up to 28 cm long.

name: Steppe bison
fact: Steppe bison were common on the Ice Age grasslands and appear often in cave paintings.

name: Diprotodon
fact: Diprotodon was the largest marsupial ever, about the size of a rhinoceros, living in Ice Age Australia.

name: Wild horse
fact: Wild horses roamed Ice Age steppes across Eurasia and North America.

name: Reindeer
fact: Reindeer (caribou in North America) migrate huge distances, and both males and females grow antlers.

name: Arctic fox
fact: Arctic foxes turn white in winter and brown-grey in summer.

name: Aurochs
fact: The aurochs, the wild ancestor of cattle, survived in Poland until 1627.

name: Deer
fact: Deer shed and regrow their antlers every year.

name: Wild boar
fact: Wild boar are the ancestors of domestic pigs and still live in forests across Eurasia.

name: Brown bear
fact: Brown bears eat berries, roots, fish and insects, and sleep through the winter in dens.

name: Wolf
fact: Wolves live in family packs. Dogs were domesticated from ancient wolves.

name: Red fox
fact: Red foxes live on more continents than any other wild carnivore.

name: Rabbit
fact: Rabbits and hares have long ears that help them hear danger and shed heat.

name: Moose
fact: Moose are the largest deer and are good swimmers.

name: Bison
fact: Tens of millions of bison once roamed the Great Plains of North America.

name: Gazelle
fact: Gazelles can run at over 60 km/h and bound high to show predators they are fit.

name: Lion
fact: Lions are the only cats that live in groups, called prides.

name: African elephant
fact: African elephants are the largest land animals alive and can recognise friends after years apart.

name: Giraffe
fact: A giraffe’s neck has the same number of bones as a human neck: seven.

name: Zebra
fact: No two zebras have exactly the same stripes.

name: Wildebeest
fact: Over a million wildebeest migrate each year through the Serengeti and Maasai Mara.

name: Hippopotamus
fact: Hippos spend the day in water to keep cool and come out at night to graze.

name: Rhinoceros
fact: Rhinoceros horn is made of keratin, the same material as your fingernails.

name: Crocodile
fact: Crocodilians have barely changed in shape since the age of dinosaurs.

name: Tiger
fact: Tigers are the largest cats and, unlike most cats, enjoy swimming.

name: Giant panda
fact: Giant pandas eat bamboo for up to 14 hours a day.

name: Red-crowned crane
fact: Red-crowned cranes dance in pairs, leaping and bowing, and are a symbol of long life in East Asia.

name: Orangutan
fact: Orangutans, whose name means "person of the forest", build a new nest in the trees every night.

name: Kangaroo
fact: Kangaroos can hop at over 50 km/h, using their tails for balance.

name: Emu
fact: Emus cannot fly, but they can run at 50 km/h and swim well.

name: Koala
fact: Koalas eat almost nothing but eucalyptus leaves and sleep up to 20 hours a day.

name: Kiwi
fact: The kiwi of Aotearoa New Zealand lays one of the largest eggs for its size of any bird.

name: Polar bear
fact: Polar bears hunt seals from the sea ice and can swim for days.

name: Walrus
fact: Walruses use their long tusks to haul themselves out of the water onto ice.

name: Musk ox
fact: Musk oxen have the warmest wool of any animal. It is called qiviut.

name: Seal
fact: Seals can dive to great depths and hold their breath for many minutes.

name: Penguin
fact: Penguins cannot fly, but they "fly" underwater with their flipper-like wings.

name: Guanaco
fact: Guanacos are the wild ancestors of llamas and live from the high Andes to Patagonia.

name: Jaguar
fact: Jaguars have the strongest bite of any big cat for their size and swim well.

name: Capybara
fact: Capybaras are the world’s largest rodents and are very calm, even with other animals.

name: Armadillo
fact: Some armadillos can roll into a tight ball protected by their shell.

name: Raccoon
fact: Raccoons have very sensitive front paws and often handle food underwater.

name: Wild turkey
fact: Turkeys were domesticated in Mesoamerica over 2,000 years ago.

name: Wild camel
fact: Camels store fat, not water, in their humps, and can go for days without drinking.

name: Monkey
fact: Monkeys live in social troops and communicate with calls, faces and gestures.

name: Flamingo
fact: Flamingos are pink because of the pigments in the algae and shrimp they eat.

name: Songbirds
fact: There are about 10,000 species of birds. Birds are the living descendants of dinosaurs.

name: Seagulls
fact: Gulls are clever birds that follow fishing boats and ships.

name: Parrots
fact: Many parrots can imitate sounds and live for over 50 years.

name: Eagle
fact: Eagles can spot prey from several kilometres away.

name: Fish
fact: Fish were swimming in Earth’s seas long before the first dinosaurs.

name: Dolphin
fact: Dolphins call each other with signature whistles that work like names.

name: Whale
fact: The blue whale is the largest animal ever known to have lived. It is bigger than any dinosaur.

name: Dog
fact: Dogs were the first domesticated animals, tamed from wolves more than 15,000 years ago.

name: Cat
fact: Cats lived alongside farmers by about 9,500 years ago. Ancient Egyptians loved and honoured them.

name: Cattle
fact: Cattle were domesticated from the wild aurochs about 10,500 years ago in the Near East and separately in South Asia.

name: Sheep
fact: Sheep were first domesticated in the Near East about 11,000 years ago, at first for meat and later for wool.

name: Goat
fact: Goats were among the first animals domesticated, in the Zagros Mountains about 10,000 years ago.

name: Pig
fact: Pigs were domesticated from wild boar, separately in the Near East and in China.

name: Chicken
fact: Chickens descend from the red junglefowl of Southeast Asia.

name: Ducks
fact: Ducks were domesticated in China for their eggs and meat.

name: Horse
fact: Horses were domesticated on the steppes and transformed travel, farming and trade.

name: Donkey
fact: Donkeys were domesticated in northeast Africa about 7,000 years ago and carried loads on trade routes.

name: Camel
fact: Dromedary camels made long caravan journeys across the Sahara and Arabia possible.

name: Bactrian camel
fact: Two-humped Bactrian camels carried goods along the Silk Roads through cold deserts.

name: Llama
fact: Llamas were domesticated in the Andes and carried goods along mountain roads.

name: Alpaca
fact: Alpacas are raised for their soft, warm fleece.

name: Guinea pig
fact: Guinea pigs were domesticated in the Andes about 7,000 years ago.

name: Yak
fact: Yaks thrive at high altitudes on the Tibetan Plateau and provide milk, wool and transport.

name: Water buffalo
fact: Water buffalo help plough flooded rice paddies across Asia.

name: Asian elephant
fact: Asian elephants have smaller ears than African elephants and have worked alongside people for thousands of years.

name: Turkey
fact: Turkeys were domesticated in Mesoamerica and kept by the Maya and Aztecs.

name: Pigeons
fact: Homing pigeons can find their way home from hundreds of kilometres away.

name: Herded reindeer
fact: Reindeer herding has been practised by Sámi, Nenets and other Arctic peoples for centuries.

name: Robo-hound
fact: Imagined: friendly robot companions that help carry things and guide visitors.

name: Garden drone
fact: Imagined: little drones that pollinate gardens and water rooftop farms.

name: Glow moths
fact: Imagined: bioluminescent moths that light far-future gardens at night.

name: Restored mammoth
fact: Imagined: far-future scientists and Arctic communities help mammoth-like elephants return to the tundra.
